working:
$2y^2+1=2y+5\Rightarrow y=-1,2$. $A=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2}\big[(2y+5)-(2y^2+1)\big]dy=\left[-\dfrac{2y^3}{3}+y^2+4y\right]_{-1}^{2}=9$.

Independent check: Intersections satisfy 2y² + 1 = 2y + 5, giving y = -1, 2. Between them, the line is to the right, so area = ∫₋₁² [(2y + 5) − (2y² + 1)] dy = 9.
solution:
The curves intersect at $2y^2+1=2y+5$, giving $y=-1,2$. Between these limits, the line lies to the right of the parabola.
$$A=\int_{-1}^{2}\big[(2y+5)-(2y^2+1)\big]dy=\left[-\frac{2y^3}{3}+y^2+4y\right]_{-1}^{2}=9.$$
